29 September 2026, 10:00–10:30 (UTC−04:00). Hold only; the prospective utility has not confirmed its participants.

1. Maintenance process before FieldKest: 5 minutes.
2. Avoiding repeated collection of field material: 10 minutes.
3. Learning the support route: 10 minutes.

documents.name: op-books-guide
documents.title: Operations books: local reading guide
documents.text:
# Operations books: August 3–September 13, 2026

These books retain the plant round handovers and selected morning distribution routes for six weeks. Overnight plant turns finish on September 14. They are not a complete attendance or payroll record. The books include filter-run time, differential-head observations and completed routine wash entries. Other process readings remain in the operating log; field identity visits do not create billing readings.

Plant turns run 06:00–14:00, 14:00–22:00 and 22:00–06:00. Four crews rotate two turns of each kind, followed by two rest days. The named lead checks the round entries before handover. Amara Fennard joins accompanied River rounds after her August 26 induction; independent local sign-off is pending. Mina's September 9 night turn is covered by the remaining crew so daytime preparation and the September 10 outreach rehearsal stay clear.

Distribution duty runs 07:00–15:00 on weekdays. Twenty people form ten pairs in each district; two remain on depot relief. The morning visit is only part of the duty. Briefing, outward travel, returns, meal breaks, stores work and afternoon practice fit around it. Vans and kits are held 08:00–12:30. The lead drives. Owen's lead is an experienced distribution technician and retains the operational decision.

Field Desk appointments record an agreed service-desk window; the organizer manages the booking and does not attend. A no-access return does not verify a meter. These visits inspect identity and approach only: no billable reading, meter exchange, supply interruption, valve operation or confined-space entry. Account references are included to route the return correctly. Names, contact details, preferences and balances remain with Customer Service.

Sample entries stop at receipt of the sealed package. Use the sample reference for laboratory work; the field return is not a water-quality result. A maintenance request acknowledges an observed condition. Receipt by Maintenance does not mean a repair has been scheduled or completed. Small marking and housekeeping work completed by the field pair is described in the visit return.

Stock is counted in each, with physical opening, issue, return and closing quantities. A returned empty sleeve is waste, not usable stock. Training records describe observed supervised practice, not qualifications. Keep later decisions on a dated new record rather than rewriting an earlier handover.

documents.name: service-register-guide
documents.title: Customer Accounts: opening register and joins
documents.text:
# Customer Accounts: opening register and joins

Owner: Customer Accounts. Revision 1, September 15, 2026.

The opening financial position is July 1, 2026, at 18:00 (UTC−04:00). Contact and
preference views include accepted changes through September 15. Opening balances
remain historical: do not replace them with later receipts or contact changes.
This is the opening register and its account-service history, not the complete
July–September billing run. The only later financial entries included here are
Talvern's two already-settled July deliveries, retained with their delivery references.

An account is a payer relationship. A customer is its named holder; the account
contact is the person authorized to correspond. A service point is a physical
water connection. A meter measures a supply or checks part of it. None of those
is a count of residents. Customers do not acquire staff or plant access by
appearing in this register.

Use account_id to join accounts, contacts, preferences, account-services,
invoices, receipts, opening-balances, changes and cases. Use service_point_id
for service points, relationships, meters and invoice lines. Meter readings join
on meter_id; usage lines identify their exact start and end reading IDs. Tariff
and period IDs identify the effective version and the interval, never a display
label. IDs remain stable after a postal or display-name correction.

Each customer in this opening register has one billing account. Some accounts
serve multiple points. Relationships have inclusive start and exclusive end
dates; a blank end is current. A contact preference does not transfer liability.
Display corrections preserve the customer ID. Account closure, new occupiers,
physical disconnection and changes of service responsibility require their own
records; none should be inferred from these preference cases.

Population estimates count occupied dwellings at service points. They are
planning counts, not named resident records. Pine: 33,750 dwellings and 90,000
residents. River: 26,250 dwellings and 70,000 residents. Each district's homes
include houses and 25-dwelling apartment buildings. A building owner receives
the master bill; the utility does not also bill those apartments individually.

Field colleagues receive service points, meters and readings. The customer
register, balances and correspondence stay with authorized Customer Accounts
staff. Procurement sees the relevant commercial agreement, not the residential
contact register. A statement may be given to its verified account contact;
whole register exports must never be attached to a customer message.

A blank phone field means no number is retained in this view. Do not manufacture
one or treat email permission as consent for a different channel. A one-off
opening-statement email is distinct from recurring bill-delivery consent.

documents.name: service-tariff-guide
documents.title: Water charges: 2026 tariff and cadence
documents.text:
# Water charges: 2026 tariff and cadence

Rate authority: ARWC-RATES-2026-01, effective January 1–December 31, 2026.
Reference retained: ARWC-RATES-2025-01. The listed 2025 and 2026 rates are unchanged;
the annual version IDs identify the authority applying to a consumption period.
Rates apply equally in Pine and River. Currency is USD. These water tariffs have
zero tax and contain no wastewater charge. Wastewater remains a separate municipal
service. These are the approved ARWC charges, not a general tax or legal guide.

| Class | Fixed charge | Measured water | Cadence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HOME | USD 24.00 per service point | USD 1.40/m³ | Calendar quarter |
| MASTER | USD 24.00 per occupied dwelling | USD 1.40/m³ | Calendar quarter |
| BUSINESS | USD 18.00 per service point | USD 1.65/m³ | Calendar month |
| MUNICIPAL | USD 18.00 per service point | USD 1.65/m³ | Calendar month |
| SEASONAL | None | USD 1.15/m³ | Accepted delivery |

Quarterly and monthly invoices are dated the first day after the period and are
due 20 days later. Period end is exclusive: the reading at that boundary closes
the old period and may open the next. Do not create an invoice merely because a
future billing-period row exists. The opening residential period is ARWC-2026-Q2;
business and municipal opening periods are ARWC-2026-M06. ARWC-2026-Q3 and
ARWC-2026-M09 remain open at the September 16 snapshot.

Usage is the accepted end register minus the accepted start register, multiplied
by the meter multiplier. Registers and invoiced volumes are in m³. Each fixed
or usage line is rounded half up to two decimal places; sum the rounded lines
for the invoice. No estimated readings or rollover are present in the opening
interval. Both parallel feeds count; a downstream private check meter does not.
Meter exchanges contribute two non-overlapping intervals and one fixed charge
for the service point. Replacement meters start at zero, not the removed value.

The opening dataset includes paid, part-paid, unpaid and credit accounts. A
receipt and an allocation are different records. The amount allocated may not
exceed the receipt or invoice. Credit stays unapplied until a later allocation
or authorized refund; a negative balance is not an extra charge. No late charge,
interest, deposit, tax or unexplained balance-forward is part of this opening.

Talvern has a separate discretionary allowance, ARWC-W-SEASONAL-2026-v1,
under A-B-002-AGR-01: up to 7,500 m³ each June–September season, only for shared
Pine facilities. It is billed per accepted delivery, due 14 days after delivery.
The accepted June 12 delivery is 450 m³ (USD 517.50); July 2 is 620 m³
(USD 713.00); July 20 is 500 m³ (USD 575.00). All three are settled. Season-to-date
use is 1,570 m³, leaving an allowance ceiling of 5,930 m³, subject to availability.
That ceiling is not a reservation or a promise of further supply.

documents.name: service-meter-guide
documents.title: Meter relationships and opening reads
documents.text:
# Meter relationships and opening reads

Owner: Meter services. September 15, 2026.

There are 50,460 active water service points. The 51,210 active meters comprise
51,060 supply meters used for billing and 150 private check meters. The register
also retains 120 removed supply meters. Its 51,330 meter records are devices,
not service points or customers.

The 600 premises with parallel supply feeds have two billable meters. Add those
volumes once, but charge one fixed service-point amount. At 150 apartment
buildings the downstream check meter has parent_meter_id pointing at the supply
meter. Its owner is the building owner; exclude it from every invoice. A master
building's fixed tariff uses its 25 occupied dwellings, not its device count.

The 120 exchanges run from May 4 through June 12, four planned exchanges per
weekday. Each retains the old removal reading and the new installation reading
at the same instant (UTC−04:00). The old interval is closed there;
the new interval begins there. predecessor_id links the devices; supply_path
stays constant. Serial numbers never move from one physical device to another.
The historical installation read predates the opening interval; it is not a
second billable start reading for that period.

The early device installation records do not claim that the current account
holder occupied the site at installation. Service infrastructure can predate
the payer relationship. The opening consumption interval falls inside the
current account's service responsibility in every case.

Talvern's supply register records each accepted delivery cumulatively. Its
July 1 opening read equals the settled June 12 read because there was no
intervening delivery. July 2 and July 20 advance that same register. Do not
invoice the July 1 observation in addition to the accepted delivery intervals.

Period-boundary actual readings are scheduled remote register snapshots, not
simultaneous visits by a field crew. Installation and exchange readings are
recorded on site. A register timestamp does not imply continuous plant access.

These retail meters measure supplied water. They are not reservoir process
tags, engineering calibration records, or allocation-model exports. Route IDs
organize meter-service work; they do not confer control-system authority.

documents.name: service-contact-guide
documents.title: Contact changes and copies
documents.text:
# Contact changes and copies

Customer Accounts, September 15, 2026.

Ask what should change before saving a preference. A one-off paper copy, recurring
paper bills and routine service letters are three different requests. A postal
routing note does not move a water connection. A name-spacing correction does
not add a new person or transfer responsibility.

Use the verified account contact. Record the clarification, the customer's
answer, the field before and after, and the effective time. Never request a
bank statement or full bank details to find a payment: the dated receipt
reference is enough for these opening-account checks.

A routine contact window is a preference, not an appointment. Urgent service
information is not held until the preferred window. Large print has no charge.
A paper-copy queue entry means queued; it does not prove dispatch or delivery.
The retained ten copy requests are still queued in these case records.

For a meter-label question, distinguish the supply meter from a private check
meter. For a second site, confirm whether responsibility changed before
explaining the combined bill. An account explanation must not silently amend a
reading, add a charge or move a service point between districts.

documents.text:
# Community water-service explanation — preparation

Owen Vardell • 9 September 2026 • Draft for rehearsal

The original outline tried to cover source water, treatment, distribution,
customer service, the company merger, and the difference between several teams.
It is too long for the short explanation we have been asked to prepare.

For the rehearsal, I want to test a simpler opening: what happens before water
reaches our tap?

I need to check the old district terminology with Mina before using any of it.
It may be more history than the audience needs for this explanation. Rosa can
help decide what the opening question should lead to next.

One comparison that may work is a relay: different people contribute different
parts of a continuous service. I want to keep it accurate without making it
sound as though one job only begins after another team has stopped working.

documents.name: a-outreach-outline
documents.title: Before water reaches the tap
documents.text:
# Before water reaches the tap

Community session outline • Agreed at rehearsal, 10 September 2026

**Opening question:** What happens before water reaches our tap?

Explain that ARWC looks after a connected service: obtaining source water,
treating it, keeping the distribution system working, and helping customers
understand the service they receive. People with different skills do those jobs
alongside one another.

Owen's relay comparison is useful for explaining that different responsibilities
contribute to the same result. Make clear that the work continues throughout
the day; one department does not finish permanently when another takes over.

Use an everyday example such as arranging a meter visit. A customer-service
colleague helps agree the appointment, field staff do the practical work, and
the account records the result. Leave time for the audience's questions.

The separate Pine and River services joined in 2009. Mention that history if
it helps answer a question, rather than making it the introduction everyone
must sit through.

Mina has checked the explanation's accuracy. Rosa has helped with its order.
Owen will practise the shorter version. The community session's final date
remains to be arranged.

documents.name: a-billing-explanation
documents.title: Which period does my water bill cover?
documents.text:
# Which period does my water bill cover?

Customer-service explanation • Accepted 15 September 2026

The billing period is the interval identified on your bill. It tells you which
part of your service history the bill covers. The date a bill is issued is a
separate date and can be later than the end of that interval.

Your bill identifies the readings used to calculate metered consumption and
whether a reading is actual or estimated. If a date or reading is unclear,
customer service can explain the entries on your individual account.

When contacting us, tell us which bill and which part you would like explained.
There is no need to reconstruct our internal process before asking the question.
We can explain the billing period first, then discuss how the relevant reading
was obtained or applied if that would help.

For an appointment concerning your meter, customer service will work with the
appointments team to agree the practical arrangements. A question about your
bill does not itself book a meter visit.

documents.name: a-refurbishment-history
documents.title: The treatment refurbishment 2021–2023
documents.text:
# The treatment refurbishment, 2021–2023

Staff induction background • September 2026

The refurbishment was completed in planned stages while the service continued.
It is an achievement involving operations, maintenance, engineering, planning,
and the colleagues who kept other routine work moving at the same time.

Public reporting recorded progress and the completed result. Staff who worked
through the stages remember the practical coordination: preparing work, fitting
it around existing responsibilities, asking questions early, and leaving a
useful account for the people taking over.

The induction programme should give newer colleagues an opportunity to meet
some of the people behind the work and ask what the experience was like.
The practical arrangements still need to be discussed with the staff involved.

A colleague who joined after 2023 may know the completed facilities without
knowing their history. Both experiences belong in the company. Nobody needs to
have been here for a particular project to take pride in the service now.

documents.name: a-company-and-governance
documents.title: Your regional water company
documents.text:
# Your regional water company

Staff and public reference • September 2026

Alterra Regional Water Company is jointly owned by Pine and River municipal
districts and serves approximately 160,000 residents and local businesses.
The company formed in 2009 by bringing the districts' water-service functions
together. It supplies drinking water from source through treatment and
distribution, including household billing and meter services. Wastewater remains
with separate municipal services.

The owners appoint a joint board with district representatives and independent
members. The board considers the service plan, budget, and rate proposals through
the public approval process. A general manager leads the company. The director
of regional operations, Luc Venn-Morel, reports to the general manager and
presents the service implications of major operational decisions.

Pine and River remain service and cost centres within one company. Shared costs
follow the agreed allocation method. District-specific commitments are accounted
for against the district receiving the specified service. Joint ownership does
not mean every charge is automatically split equally.

Water charges support ordinary operations and planned renewal. Longer-lived
projects have separately approved capital funding. Annual service results,
board reporting, explanations to customers, and consultation over planned work
are part of the company's normal public responsibilities.

ARWC has about 230 staff. Our next five-year programme combines steady renewal,
workforce development, and service for modest regional growth. The aim is a
service the next generation can maintain and customers can continue to rely on.

documents.name: a-working-at-arwc
documents.title: Working at ARWC
documents.text:
# Working at ARWC

Staff induction reference • September 2026

| Function | Colleagues | Work |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Operations, treatment, and distribution | 94 | Plant work, field operations, service, and shift handovers |
| Maintenance and engineering | 48 | Inspections, projects, equipment condition, and commissioning |
| Planning, quality, and compliance | 32 | Demand, allocation, laboratory work, quality, and reporting |
| Information technology | 12 | Business applications, identity, integration, and internal services |
| Customer service and business support | 36 | Accounts, procurement, records, correspondence, and scheduling |
| Leadership and finance | 8 | Governance, budgets, finance, and organizational leadership |

Our service has overlapping working days. Some colleagues work plant shifts,
some travel between field assignments, and others provide customer-service or
office coverage. Check those arrangements when organizing a meeting or staff
event. Main-office hours do not describe everyone's day.

Most operational and customer-service positions are covered by established
collective agreements. Management and some professional roles have separate
employment arrangements. Your manager and the appropriate staff representative
can explain the arrangements for your position.

Development can mean deeper technical expertise, training work, a different
specialism, or a supervisory role. Apprentices work through planned assignments
under supervision. They arrive with different prior experience and should feel
able to ask questions, including asking for an explanation a second time.

Experienced colleagues also have development goals. Planning for succession
includes time to prepare and teach, as well as the teaching session itself.
Long service is not a substitute for asking somebody about their plans.

Voluntary staff activities include the autumn photography display and staff
walk. Some colleagues participate; others have different interests or commitments.
There are many ways to belong to the company.

documents.name: a-regional-history
documents.title: Becoming a regional service
documents.text:
# Becoming a regional service

Records and staff induction note • September 2026

Before 2009, Pine and River operated separate water services. Bringing them
together made it possible to share planning, purchasing, and management while
local depots continued their practical work. It also allowed the company to
develop specialist expertise that the districts had often bought separately.

The change took time. Staff learned colleagues' routines, and records retained
names and descriptions from the services that produced them. Some of those
names still occur in conversation. Many employees joined after the merger and
identify more strongly with their team or profession than a predecessor service.

Between 2014 and 2017, staged distribution renewal completed several neighbourhood
jobs that staff still remember with pride. Customer service adopted common
account procedures during 2018–2019. FieldKest was introduced during the same
period for selected external handovers, reducing repeated collection of records.

The treatment refurbishment completed between 2021 and 2023 is another shared
achievement. More recently, training and succession have received attention as
experienced employees consider their next career stages. The 2025 apprentice
intake is part of that continuing development.

The staff-history scanning project has preserved photographs and other material
from earlier offices. Descriptions identify where and when an item belongs so
someone can understand it without finding a colleague who remembers it personally.

documents.name: a-regional-service
documents.title: Regional service and customer relationships
documents.text:
# Regional service and customer relationships

Customer-service reference • September 2026

Most customers encounter ARWC through their ordinary water service, bills, meter
appointments, planned work, and information about seasonal use. Municipal
facilities are customers alongside households and businesses.

Cairn Reach Reservoir is one important reserve within a wider source portfolio.
ARWC also has an established supplementary bulk-supply agreement with Merewick
Bulk Water Cooperative. Merewick serves neighbouring systems from a larger,
different source and storage portfolio. ARWC is a contract customer, rather
than a member owner. Available deliveries depend on Merewick's commitments and
conditions, and are limited by the agreement.

Belvarn Packaging is a River district manufacturer whose shorter production
runs make clear scheduling useful. Its staff are considering an efficiency
project and ask practical questions about metering and ordinary bills. Belvarn
also works with the local training college on apprenticeships.

Talvern Growers Cooperative represents Pine district growers, including nurseries
and producers of high-value horticultural crops. ARWC provides a limited,
supplementary seasonal irrigation allowance through the treated distribution
service. Members' other water arrangements are outside that contract. Talvern
helps members understand the allowance and arrange common information sessions.

Different customers need different explanations. A useful response starts with
the question they asked and the service involved. Customer-service staff can
bring in planning or other colleagues when a question needs their expertise.
